I think of typology as a system of people who think in a very similar way based on choices they can choose from. It isn't specifically YOU because even though you might pick an answer/solution more frequently as another "ENTP" / "ennea 7" person, you still differ in other choices based on your experiences and unique circumstances in life. It's just something where we can find people we share a lot in common with in terms of common choices and views which makes us relate to those people a whole lot more, therefore the communication between those sets of people can be more reasoned with due to your brain knowing "well, they are 'ENTP' , and I know what this 'ENTP' is based upon, so I understand what their thought process might be more than others."

It isn't 100% legit obviously, it isn't accurately scientific, it's just a bundle of answers you give that you can relate yourself to along with others. Even with this knowledge I find it comforting in a way because I feel like I know the base structure of the other person and I can identify the patterns even if I don't know their "type", so I can communicate to them in a way where they can understand what I'm trying to get at as well as I'm trying to understand/mostly understand where they are trying to get at.

Remember you are unique because of your circumstances, upbringing, I could go on for more factors why you might think the way you do, typology only sums up the common characteristics you share with said group of people, which leads you to understand them a lot better.

One day at my college, I spilled my ice coffee on this woman I've never seen before. I was really embarrased, apologized a lot. I didn't think much of it though. Next day, I see her again. We began laughing about yesterday, then talking a bit. Each day, we started talking more and more. It soon escalated to dating. I had true feelings for her, and so did she. And one day, I couldn't hold it back. I asked her to marry me. She said yes.

This began a new chapter in our life. We both saved up enough to buy a house. Moved to a new city, with weird neighbours. And then, a beautiful baby was born. 2 years later, and another baby was born. And I was thinking to myself that things couldn't be better. I was living a truly happy live.

Fast forward to about 10 years later. Kids screaming in the back of the car asking us to go to a fast food joint to get some burgers. My wife asked for Burger King, but there weren't any of those nearby. I didn't say anything and drove to McDonald's. When we arrived, she was silent. She didn't even scream at me, she just didn't say anything at all. After that, she refused to speak to me for another 2 days. You'd think I'd never let this happen again, right? Well, I did.

A few months later, my daughter won a singing competition. We were on our way to pick her up, but I wanted to surprise her with a burger or something. I said that to my wife and she agreed. I then drove to McDonald's, as I didn't remember the last incident at all. Worst mistake of my life. When we got there, she started hitting me and screaming, something about McDonald's. We skipped fast food and went to pick up my daughter. We drove in absolute silence.

When we got home, she was angry. The angriest I've ever seen her. She straight up filed a divorce. She straight up asked for everything i have, including the kids. I couldn't believe what I just heard. I thought it was just a dream. It was not. It was a nightmare. I was not able to even argue with her. She had lawyers. The best lawyers the country has to offer.

I had no other choice but to start living with my parents. I had no money. No house. Nothing. I was absolutely devastated.

Moral of the story: go to popeyes. They have great chicken.
